card.name: NSA Surveillance Backdoor
card.lore: The government doesn't need to crack your password when Big Tech leaves the back door wide open and the porch light on.
card.power: Reads everything, regardless of your cute encryption.

interpretation.summary: The card compresses different surveillance mechanisms into an all-seeing backdoor. That is a dramatic premise; the inspected report supports a narrower collection process. The NB01 infographic is useful as a question map, not proof of blanket access. Neither this report nor a product label establishes that every encrypted message is readable.
interpretation.counterposition: Avoid both total-immunity promises and the claim that nothing helps. Protection depends on the data, adversary and access mechanism.

brainfood.text: Step right up: the all-seeing machine comes with a very blurry instruction manual. Name the data. Name the doorway. Then check who actually holds the key.
brainfood.voiceBasis: Carny concrete exhibit/direct address + KnuckleBob paper/trail/mechanism, from inventoried FrizzleBob voice donors. New prose, not copied source assertions.

solutionWatch.action: Spend ten minutes making a one-data-item security plan before buying a new phone.
steps: Choose one item: private messages, location history or documents.
List where it is stored, who can access it and the specific access you want to reduce.
Choose one proportionate change, then set a review date.

options.name: Keep the current device and review one unnecessary app permission
options.advantage: No new hardware cost; bounded and reversible.
options.limit: Does not remove every provider-held record or address every adversary.

options.name: Compare a different communication/service workflow against the same threat
options.advantage: Tests whether a change actually addresses the chosen exposure.
options.limit: Compatibility, contacts and migration effort matter; encryption and endpoints need separate review.

options.name: Consider alternative hardware/OS only after the threat comparison
options.limit: Above Phone, Volla and other products are leads, not tested recommendations in this pilot; no promise of anonymity.

solutionWatch.funding: No paid placement or affiliate links introduced.
solutionWatch.successCheck: You can explain one threat, one chosen mitigation and one remaining limitation.
solutionWatch.notProvided: No purchase verdict or individual legal/security guarantee.

claims.statement: The PCLOB2023 report describes downstream collection through identified selectors at service providers, distinct from upstream collection.
claims.reviewScope: See exact source receipts; no assertion beyond read passages.

dialogueExample.question: Can the NSA read everything?
dialogueExample.answer: That universal claim is not established here. The inspected PCLOB2023 passage describes selector-based downstream collection; other access mechanisms require separate sources.
